in.reason: wants to play closer to home

out.name: Yuna Su-Seong
out.reason: wants to play closer to home

teams.note: Thirty-one first-place votes for a team that UNN beat twice in the same postseason: 31-16 in the Great Fourteen final and 38-20 in the second round, which closed a 10-5 year. The voters are betting on what stayed. Ximena Coldcombe, Taeyang Su-Won and Vesna Karakos are sophomores with a full season behind them, and five-star tailback Nemiy Tomselniy arrives in the same offseason that Heriberto Campovieja went in round one, one of three from the program taken there. Boris Walker's eighth year goes through North Hatesei on the road in week 5, Ranroman at home in week 6, Kaji Daun in week 11, and UNN in week 14.

teams.name: Skylar Rose

in.name: Wanda Kamenanov
in.reason: wants to play closer to home

teams.note: The champions, 16-1 after a 49-10 title game over UFNH, take twenty-six first-place votes and the second spot. Alessia Verville, who threw for 418 yards and six touchdowns against Dietsche in the quarterfinals, is a sophomore now; Maximo Penalarga is a senior on the defensive line and Itzel Torrabella is a five-star tailback arriving to follow Lubna El-Nadim, a third-round pick. Amir Chen's sixth year opens a new defensive coordinator, Kadhim El-Kubaisi, in from Perth Island. The test comes early: Tengus State on the road in week 3, then Park Island at home in a rematch of the Western Coast final.

teams.name: Eona

in.name: Tsuvai Eiselniy
in.reason: one shot at a bigger stage

teams.note: A 10-4 year ended in the second round, 31-27 to Eastern State on a touchdown with 44 seconds left. Offensive coordinator DeAndre Kingsbrook left to run German Shores, and Pietro Montichelli takes over the offense. The headline arrival is Tsuvai Eiselniy, a 999-yard receiver from Will Tech, along with five-star defensive lineman Alessia Boischamp; quarterback Dragana Eichenbauer went in round three. Hollis Upshaw's fourth year has UNN at home in week 5 and Kaji Daun at home in week 8, and a week-13 trip to Ranroman.

teams.name: Skeenerland State

in.name: Gudrun Gradkov
in.reason: one shot at a bigger stage

teams.note: Twelve wins, a Power North final lost 17-11 to Kaji Kita, and a semifinal that turned in the fourth quarter: 20-20 against Skylar Rose before an 87-yard pick-six. The quarterback is the question. Abiodun El-Ghazali, 406 yards and four touchdowns in the quarterfinal win over Verigon, went 26th overall, and Mikhail Ananidis arrives from North Canesta. Michio Sugita, a five-star receiver, headlines a class tied for the best in the country by star total. Ji-woo Hall's twelfth year includes a week-11 trip to Kaji Kita, the team that beat them for the division.

teams.name: Eastern State

in.name: Bora Xiongding
in.reason: wants to play closer to home

in.name: Cecily Eastbrook
in.reason: didn't fit the new staff's plans

teams.note: The 2040 champions went 12-3, lost the Broad South final 15-14 in the rain to Ciarralotta Tech and its kicker, and in the playoff beat Eona before losing to UNN in the snow. Boubacar Grimaldi went 27th overall and Tamsin Bellac, a cornerback, went in round one as well. Bhaskar El-Mahdi's second year brings a new offensive coordinator in Tengfei Shiraura, last seen as head coach at Dove Island State, and a quarterback room that includes Percy Darwish, a four-star freshman, and Cecily Eastbrook, in from Roosevelt Mines. Nemiy Havmark, who had 214 yards and three touchdowns against Eona, returns at receiver.

teams.name: Tengus State

in.name: Emeka Eastmond
in.reason: wants to play closer to home

teams.note: A 9-4 year with an uneven edge: Northlight beat them in overtime in week 3 and Skeenerland State came back from 21-0 down to win 23-21 in week 12. Layla Smith's fourteenth year brings a new offensive coordinator, Sybil Inglethorpe, from Roosevelt, and a quarterback transfer in Emeka Eastmond, from Tengus. Five-star receiver Mireille Grijalva arrives in the same offseason that Ofa Taumalu went in round four, and Barnaby Kingsbank, a safety, went in round two. Skylar Rose visits in week 3 and Kaji Kita hosts in week 4, which will say a lot early.

teams.name: UNN

out.name: Callum Malchamp
out.reason: one shot at a bigger stage

teams.note: Twelve wins, the Great Fourteen title, a 38-20 win over Central Stanton in the second round in which Svyatoslav Tetteng threw for 463 yards and five touchdowns, and a 24-0 loss to UFNH in the semifinal. Tetteng is a senior now. Tight end Chidinma Owusowah went in round one and George Thorvaldsen in round two, and five-star linebacker Zbigniew Chidambaram arrives. Esperanza Caraobruno's fourth year faces the toughest slate of opponents in the country on paper: Dietsche in week 1, then Eona away in week 5, North Hatesei at home in week 6, Ranroman away in week 7, and Kaji Daun away in week 9.

teams.name: Ranroman
teams.note: An 8-5 year ended at Rogaela, 24-9, in the first round. Ghislaine Penahermosa's second year has new options at quarterback in Jalen Eastman, a four-star freshman, and Cristobal Rowbank, a transfer from Southeastern, and the receivers lost Prokopis Eastworth in round one. Urmila Jayawardhan starts a tenth year as defensive coordinator, and the class of twenty ranks fourth in the country by star total. The Great Fourteen gauntlet is concentrated: at Central Stanton in week 6, UNN at home in week 7, North Hatesei at home in week 10, and Eona at home in week 13.

teams.name: North Hatesei

in.name: Corrado Qiza
in.reason: wants to play closer to home

in.name: Porfirio Borinsky
in.reason: wants to play closer to home

teams.note: A 6-6 year, 4-5 in the conference, and then the coaching staff came apart. Offensive coordinator Lorenzo Verbois left to run Costique and defensive coordinator Porfirio Zanetti to run North Verigon; Tamika Anynna, from Holliday, and Tessa Onyeemeka, from Orlot, take over. Only two players were drafted, Lakshman Oakwood in round five and Lionel Clayshaw in round six, and linebacker Mstislav Chernyshyn and safety Noemie Cataldo are sophomores. The last title came in 2030, and Meera Moreau's fourth year starts with Central Stanton at home in week 5, then UNN, Kaji Daun, and Ranroman away in weeks 6, 7 and 10.

teams.name: UFNH

in.name: Giovanni Lazzaro
in.reason: one shot at a bigger stage

teams.note: A 14-3 year that included a 24-0 semifinal over UNN, a first title-game trip, and a 49-10 loss to Skylar Rose. The Mountain Valley final went the other way too, 24-14 to Verigon. Georgia Apopoulos, four sacks against UNN, went in round one; Paloma Fontoncelli went in round five and Reinhold Rosenholz, a kicker, in round four. Wapasha Lamedeer arrives at quarterback from Costique, and Verity Hyun-Nam is a five-star defensive lineman. Moritz Lamehawk's second year has Verigon at home in week 11, Crayellan at home in week 13, and a week-14 trip to Fiota Bay, who lost to them 34-31 on a late touchdown.

teams.name: Ranroman State

in.name: Lamont Achebe
in.reason: one shot at a bigger stage

teams.note: A 6-6 year, 3-6 in the Great Fourteen, and still eleventh on the ballots. Keyto Kovaw, a linebacker, went in round one, and the transfers include defensive lineman Lamont Achebe from Hatesei and safeties Sybil Kingshurst and Rin Moritsu, in from Rogaela Tech and Tengus; wide receiver Antoine Readgate left for Eternal Fox. Litowa Mesteniy's third year has the third-toughest slate of opponents in the country on paper, with Crayellan away in week 1, Kaji Daun away in week 4, UNN away in week 10 and Ranroman at home to close in week 14.

teams.name: Kaji Kita
teams.note: Eleven wins, a 17-11 win over Skeenerland State for the Power North title, a 19-16 second-round win over Fiota Bay, and then a 30-17 quarterfinal loss to UFNH. Ernest Fjelldahl, the defensive player of the year with 19 sacks, is back as a junior, and five-star safety Peymyr Virsemyr arrives. Ebony Anywale's third year keeps Efua Kofbuike as offensive coordinator, a thirteenth year in the role. Barhold on the road in week 3, Tengus State at home in week 4, and Skeenerland State at home in week 11 are the dates that decide the division again.

teams.name: Ciarralotta Tech
teams.note: Nine wins and a very Ciarralotta Tech way of getting them: a 15-14 Broad South final over Eastern State on Deepika El-Husri's field goals in the rain, then a 35-34 first-round loss to Dietsche in a game where Nneka Ugonti threw for 441 yards and four touchdowns. Both are back. Wanda Borovec, a safety, went first overall to Queensville, and Alfie Holmhus and Maelys Lundvoll followed in round two. Uili Tendulkar's fourth year has a new defensive coordinator, Yui Nishiyama, from Riveral, a class tied for the best by star total, and Ciarralotta State in week 14.

teams.name: Park Island
teams.note: Eleven wins, a 28-24 loss to Skylar Rose in the Western Coast final, and a 34-9 second-round loss at home to Dietsche. Norbert Ackerwetter went in round one, Diamond Coleberry in round two and Huiling Seo-Seong, who had 371 receiving yards against Yrei Trobniy in week 9, in round three, and Amira Tzavellas comes in from Far Farris. Hosei Mesysei is a five-star tailback. Svetlana Wright's fourth year opens at Marines in week 1, brings Barhold State in week 3, and puts the rematch with Skylar Rose at Skylar Rose in week 4.

teams.name: Crayellan
teams.note: Eight wins, 6-3 in Mountain Valley, and left out of the 24-team field along with eleven-win Coastal Ranroman. The year had its high points, 41-0 over UFNH in week 7 and a 30-9 win at Verigon in week 8, and its low one, a 45-10 loss to Fiota Bay and Zaire Winswick in week 9. Ximena Carrasco's fifth year has Kanei Tomtrovaw, a senior linebacker, back, and Mamadou Gangalingam gone in round two. Ranroman State visits in week 1, Fiota Bay in week 9, and UFNH is the week-13 trip.

teams.name: Rogaela State

out.name: Nikhil Al-Husri
out.reason: wants to play closer to home

teams.note: Last year's preseason number one, with twenty-three first-place votes, went 6-6 and 3-6 in Jyras Bay, and the draft took six more, among them Itsuki Nagamaki and Hwanki Kurobashi in round one and Kwame Folamah in round two. What's left: Maisie Althauer at tailback, a sophomore who rushed for 128 yards and two touchdowns in a win over Leafette as a freshman, and a defense with Haeun Asaura and Noor Chisei back. Rami Campbell starts year fifteen with two coordinators in their second year, Carlos Lopez and Anaru Manutai, and a week-3 trip to Central Stanton.

teams.name: Kaji Daun

in.reason: one shot at a bigger stage

out.reason: wants to play closer to home

out.name: Beatrice Blauberger
out.reason: wants to play closer to home

teams.note: A year after opening fourth in the preseason poll, 4-8, with three straight losses in the middle and a coach, Fatima Larsen, gone before the season finished. Henrik Moreau is the head coach in his second year. Ruolan Xuegang, an offensive lineman, went in round one, with Alofa Kickinghorn and Anais Navanegro following in rounds two and three, and the transfer class is thin: Marquis Blackbrook at receiver from Antiragal and kicker Irmgard Ulbrecht from Larksdale. The schedule does not wait: North Hatesei, Eona, and UNN in weeks 7 through 9, Central Stanton in week 11, and Kaji Kita in week 14.

teams.name: Dietsche

in.name: Alessia Bustamante
in.reason: didn't fit the new staff's plans

teams.note: Eleven wins and a quarterfinal run: a 35-34 first-round win over Ciarralotta Tech, a 34-9 win at fourth-seeded Park Island, and then a 52-37 loss to Skylar Rose in which Andreas El-Najjar threw for 472 yards and five touchdowns. El-Najjar is a junior and returns. Bertram Havtveit, a tight end, went in round one, and Rupert Ravenborough and Leif Winterbury followed in round six. Sora Yamamoto's fourth year opens with Sacred Tomb at home in week 0, UNN on the road in week 1, and Will Tech at home in week 2.

teams.name: Will Tech

out.name: Tsuvai Eiselniy
out.reason: one shot at a bigger stage

teams.note: A 10-4 year that ended with a 31-21 Jyras Bay final loss to South Antiragal and then a 37-24 first-round loss at home to Eternal Fox. Tsuvai Eiselniy, a 999-yard receiver, is now at Eona, and Annika Weinheim went in round one. This is a veteran roster, with seniors Harumi Ohm at receiver, Mstislav Redturtle at kicker, Lukas Bernfelder on the defensive line, and Shaniqua Gueye at punter. Wilhelmina Kleinmann's fourth year opens with Orlot at home in week 1, then Dietsche on the road in week 2.

teams.name: Verigon

in.name: Mikhail Makrimatos
in.reason: followed DC Kaito Yentravaw to Verigon

teams.note: Twelve wins and the Mountain Valley title, 24-14 over UFNH, a 31-21 second-round win over UN Minko, and a 38-29 quarterfinal loss to Skeenerland State at the Lumber Bowl. Otto Achterberg arrives at tight end from Skeenerland and Percy Nishiyama is a sophomore at the position; Cortez Hazelden, who rushed for 176 yards against UN Minko, is back at tailback, and Iosefa Halatele is a five-star offensive lineman. Bhaskar Al-Adawi's fourth year has Kaito Yentravaw, a head coach at Queensville until this offseason, as defensive coordinator, and a week-11 trip to UFNH.

teams.name: Yrei Trobniy
teams.note: Eight wins and no transfers in or out: Yrei Trobniy is the one team in the top 25 that stood pat in the portal. Sungmin Zhenbin, a five-star junior, is at quarterback again; the draft took Yantrei Miyselniy in round four, Gudrun Dulac in round five and Shota Kurooka in round seven. Hollis Heathcote's fourth year has Mirae Seok, from Keeper, as defensive coordinator. North Hatesei on the road in week 2 and Skylar Rose at home in week 9 are the dates that matter, with UN Steelbridge in between.

teams.name: Ciarralotta State

out.name: Tessa Jagannathan
out.reason: one shot at a bigger stage

teams.note: Seven wins and a 5-4 conference record, then a first-round pick in Shaniqua Maywood, an offensive lineman, and a second-round pick in Tomavaw Habibi, a tailback. Imani Latu starts a sixteenth year at the same school with a class of twenty and five blue-chip signings; Bozena Krasyshyn at safety and offensive linemen Wesley Yorkden and Sooyoung Shirabara lead the veterans. The slate that tells you what you need to know: Perth Island at home in week 1, Ciarralotta on the road in week 9, Eastern State on the road in week 11, and Ciarralotta Tech on the road in week 14.

teams.name: Eternal Fox

in.name: Yaa Brookridge
in.reason: followed DC Khalid Jayagiri to Eternal Fox

teams.note: The only team from outside the six power conferences on the ballot: an 11-4 year that included a 17-0 East Forest title game, a 37-24 first-round win at Will Tech, and a 45-23 second-round loss to Skylar Rose. Quarterback Rupert Hazelton went in round five, Sota Masunaga and Priya Al-Nadim, both tailbacks, in rounds three and five, and the quarterback options are now Yaa Brookridge, a senior from Southern Krobe, and Joaquin Penarica, a four-star freshman. Perla Notaro's fourth year has Khalid Jayagiri, from Southern Krobe, as defensive coordinator and Antoine Readgate at receiver. The one ranked opponent on the schedule is Fiota Bay, in week 2.

teams.name: Barhold

in.name: Ormyr Vessei
in.reason: didn't fit the new staff's plans

teams.note: Seven wins, 5-4 in Power North, and one draft pick, Dulce Malpre in round six. Darnell Ellery's third year has a new look through the portal: James Gyenna, a quarterback, from Keytommiyr; cornerback Adjoa Ezesah, from National; and kicker Ormyr Vessei, from Rupin State. Their class has three blue chips among fifteen signings. Kaji Kita comes to town in week 3, then Skeenerland State on the road in week 9 and Tengus State on the road in week 11.

teams.name: Fiota Bay
teams.note: Ten wins and a 19-16 second-round loss at Kaji Kita in which Zaire Winswick, the freshman of the year (3,383 yards, 30 touchdowns, 6 interceptions), threw three interceptions. Winswick, who had five touchdown passes in the 45-10 win over Crayellan, is a sophomore. Tatiana Blauholz, a tight end, went in round one. Catalina Eastwood's fifth year starts at Tasson in week 1, brings Eternal Fox in week 2, and ends with UFNH at home in week 14, a rematch of last year's 34-31 loss on a late score.
